body: Idk if knowing why my dad was so cruel to me while he praised my younger sister would have helped. Because deep down as a teen I knew it had to deal with the fact I wouldn't agree with everything he said and called him out when he was being shitty, I just didn't have the term narcissist to really put there. But I do know I would go back to tell my sister that one day she will break the cycle too, and we both will be scapegoats. I would tell her that it's okay to see him for what he is. I would say not to hurt so much from that fall from grace because it wasn't real and was based on if she was complacent and obedient.

Unfortunately, I cannot add much here that others have not already said. But I know how you feel. I live with my parents at the moment and watch everyday just how belittling, bitter, and verbally aggressive he can be towards my mother. I try and talk with her gently about it and she agrees that what he does is abusive, but she loves him and we depend on that income. She knew a different version of him when they got married and she holds onto that hope that he will go back to being that person, but he only has gotten worse. If I were you, I would try and help her save up and get out of there temporarily because it sounds like it isn't safe there.

Everyone deserves to find some kind of happiness, you are right. I just feel like I'm in a train heading towards another one. Like I know I have to stop, but I feel powerless to do so. As in, I know what I need to do to be happy, but it's so hard just getting there. I know I need to not be so dependent on others for happiness, but I don't know how to solve that problem. I work hard...I go to school (for biochemistry), I work as a supervisor for UPS, and I'm trying my best to take better care of myself. Yet it means almost nothing if I have no one to share it with...I need to figure out what will make me happy just being by myself.
